    Enrichment factor for virtual screening

    Source: R/yardstick-metrics.R
    enrichment_factor.Rd

    The enrichment factor (EF) compares the hit rate among the top-scoring fraction of a ranked list with the hit rate in the whole list. An EF of 10 at 1 percent means the top 1 percent holds ten times more actives than random selection would give. It is widely used to assess virtual screening, biomarker and protein engineering models that prioritise candidates for testing.

    Usage

    enrichment_factor(data, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
enrichment_factor(
  data,
  truth,
  ...,
  fraction = 0.01,
  na_rm = TRUE,
  event_level = "first",
  case_weights = NULL
)

enrichment_factor_vec(
  truth,
  estimate,
  fraction = 0.01,
  na_rm = TRUE,
  event_level = "first",
  case_weights = NULL,
  ...
)

    Arguments

    data

    A data frame with the truth and probability or score columns.

    ...

    The column with the predicted probability or score for the event class.

    truth

    <tidy-select> The true class (a factor with two levels).

    fraction

    Fraction of the ranked list to examine, between 0 and 1.

    na_rm

    Remove missing values before computing?

    event_level

    "first" or "second": which level of truth is the event (active).

    case_weights

    Not supported; must be NULL.

    estimate

    For the _vec() function, a numeric vector of scores.

    Value

    For the data frame method, a tibble with columns .metric, .estimator and .estimate. For enrichment_factor_vec(), a single number.

    References

    Truchon, J.-F. and Bayly, C. I. (2007). Evaluating virtual screening methods: good and bad metrics for the "early recognition" problem. Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling, 47, 488-508. doi:10.1021/ci600426e

    See also

    Other tidybiotek metrics: assay_cv_error(), bedroc()

    Examples

    set.seed(2)
screen <- tibble::tibble(
  active = factor(rep(c("yes", "no"), c(20, 480)), levels = c("yes", "no")),
  score = c(rnorm(20, 2), rnorm(480))
)
enrichment_factor(screen, active, score, fraction = 0.05)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   .metric           .estimator .estimate
#>   <chr>             <chr>          <dbl>
#> 1 enrichment_factor binary            12
